claims.text: Machine-learning-guided processing optimization can tune the magnetic behavior of low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs.
Machine-learning-guided processing optimization can tune the magnetocaloric behavior of low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs.
Optimal thermal and thickness treatments adjust the microstructure of low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs.
Conventionally synthesized low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs have a disordered microstructure.
A machine-learning framework integrating experimental magnetic and magnetocaloric measurements with multiscale simulations can predict useful thermal-treatment and thickness parameters.
Thermal treatment affects grain size, defect density, and phase-fraction distributions.
Sample thickness affects grain size, defect density, and phase-fraction distributions.
Temperature-dependent spin fluctuations affect phase stability in the target low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs.
Thermally induced changes in defect-related microstructure can arise through changes in stacking-fault energetics.
Adjusting thermal and thickness parameters alters magnetic transition characteristics.
Processing-induced changes to magnetic transition characteristics enhance the magnetocaloric response.
ML-optimized processing will shift magnetic transition temperatures relative to conventional processing.
ML-optimized processing will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to conventional processing.
ML-optimized processing will increase the magnetic entropy change relative to conventional processing.
The approach is effective primarily where microstructural descriptors are sensitive to processing conditions.
Extreme dimensions or treatments outside the modeled parameter range may not produce the predicted improvements.
